tier_1_axioms.assertion: Radiocarbon Dating Locks Vellum Creation to 1404–1438 AD
evidence: University of Arizona AMS Radiocarbon laboratory (2009).
4 independent parchment samples tested across different quires.
Calibrated 95% confidence interval yields 1404–1438 AD.
Disproves modern forgery (Wilfrid Voynich) and Elizabethan creation (John Dee/Edward Kelley).
tier_1_axioms.falsification_risk: Effectively 0% unless standard AMS physics is invalid.

tier_1_axioms.assertion: Pigments and Ink Are Authentic 15th-Century European Formulations
evidence: McCrone Research Institute micro-chemical analysis (2009).
Iron gall ink used throughout text and line drawings.
Azurite (blue), copper green / verdigris (green), cinnabar / red lead (red), orpiment (yellow).
Complete absence of modern titanium white, Prussian blue (post-1704), or synthetic pigments.

tier_1_axioms.assertion: The Codex Contains 225 Surviving Folios Across 16 Quires with Foldouts
evidence: Physical collation at Yale Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library (MS 408).
Parchment prepared from calfskin vellum.
Complex foldout sheets up to 6-panel foldouts (f85–f86 Rosettes).
Sewing holes and historical foliation indicate ~14–16 lost folios since 15th century.

tier_1_axioms.assertion: The Text Was Written Left-to-Right in Single Continuous Execution Without Corrections
evidence: Consistent, un-squeezed left margins; ragged, uneven right margins.
Currier, Tiltman, and D'Imperio palaeographic observations.
Ink stroke sequence confirms left-to-right ductus.
Complete absence of erasure marks, pen-knife scrapings, or crossed-out words.

tier_1_axioms.assertion: The Manuscript Features at Least Two Distinct Dialects / Hands (Currier A and Currier B)
evidence: Captain Prescott H. Currier's 1976 statistical paper.
Currier A dominates Herbal (f1–f66) and Zodiac (f70–f73); Currier B dominates Balneological (f75–f84) and Recipes (f103–f116).
Jaccard vocabulary overlap between Currier A and Currier B is only 0.1711 (82.9% disjunction).
Currier A features high 'o-' and 'd-' frequencies; Currier B features high 'ch-' and 'sh-' frequencies.

tier_1_axioms.assertion: Character Entropy is Abnormally Low (h2 ≈ 2.0–2.4 bits/char) While Strictly Obeying Zipf's Law
evidence: Second-order conditional character entropy is drastically lower than European languages (~4.0 bits).
Word frequencies follow Zipf's Law power-law distribution identically to natural language.
Token autocorrelation decays over long ranges (20–30 words), proving high-level topic structuring (Montemurro & Zanette 2013).
Word order is not random (scrambling text destroys these mathematical properties).

tier_1_axioms.assertion: Line-as-a-Functional-Unit Invariant (Strong Line-End and Line-Start Constraints)
evidence: Gallows glyphs (t, k, p, f) occur at the start of lines at over 4x their expected random frequency.
Terminal glyphs (-y, -m, -am) concentrate overwhelmingly at line ends.
Near-zero word hyphenation or word-splitting across line breaks.
Suggests the scribe composed or fit words specifically within line boundaries.

tier_1_axioms.assertion: The Oocephalus Invariant: Pharmaceutical Jar Labels Do NOT Match Herbal Plant Names
evidence: The Oocephalus Test (Casey & Henderson 2026).
Direct binomial test against the 80% crib rate expectation yields p = 2.54e-12.
Monte Carlo permutation yields Z = +0.631 (p = 0.528, identical to random chance).
Morphological tolerance (edit distance <= 1) yields Z = -0.41 (p = 0.738).
Disproves that pharmaceutical jar labels represent plant names of corresponding herbal folios.

tier_1_axioms.assertion: The Organ Label Invariant: Labels Are NOT Fixed Anatomical Words (Radix, Folium, Flos)
evidence: Organ Label Benchmark (Casey & Henderson 2026).
93.3% of pharmaceutical labels (139/149) are completely unique words.
Chi-squared test of prefix vs. drawn organ yields chi2 = 8.42, p = 0.751 (identical to random noise).
Disproves that labels represent generic plant organs or processing instructions.

tier_1_axioms.assertion: The Zodiac Star Invariant: Star Labels Are NOT Proper Astronomical Star Names
evidence: Zodiac Star Concordance (Casey & Henderson 2026).
359 star labels across 12 medallions share tokens across completely distinct signs (e.g. 'otal' appears 6 times in Pisces, Aries, Taurus, Scorpio).
Proper star names (Aldebaran, Regulus, Spica) cannot physically wander across constellations.
41.5% of star labels recur in the Herbal body text; 37.4% recur in Recipe Stars.
Disproves Stephen Bax's nominal star cribs.

supporting_evidence: Sectional progression matches 15th-century Tacuina Sanitatis: Simples -> Zodiac -> Baths -> Jars -> Recipes.
Balneological section depicts female hydrotherapy consistent with Galenic uterine fumigations and mineral spa regimens.
Zodiac medallions align with medieval medical astrology (bloodletting, planetary rulership of treatments).
counter_evidence: Illustrations depict idiosyncratic, non-standard plants unlike contemporary printed herbals.
Complete failure of text to match standard Latin or German pharmacological vocabulary.

supporting_evidence: Abnormally low character entropy (h2 ≈ 2.0–2.4) is a hallmark of artificial taxonomy systems.
Rigid morphemic slots (prefix-root-suffix) where prefixes categorize domains and suffixes denote states.
High token predictability and absence of irregular phonetic mutations found in natural spoken languages.
counter_evidence: Pre-dates John Wilkins (1668) and George Dalgarno (1661) by more than two centuries.
Requires an unprecedented early 15th-century linguistic pioneer.

tier_2_theories.theory: Procedural Table Generation with Scribe Memory (Markovian Device)
supporting_evidence: Explains frequent immediate word self-repetitions ('word crumbles' like chol.chol, daiin.daiin).
Explains strict line-length and margin constraints.
Explains how scribes could write thousands of words fluidly without pauses or corrections.
counter_evidence: Fails to cleanly explain Montemurro's long-range semantic keyword clustering (20–30 word horizons).
Pure mechanical generation rarely preserves cross-quire topical cohesion.

tier_2_theories.theory: Enciphered Natural Language via Homophonic Polyalphabetic Cipher
supporting_evidence: Fifteenth-century Italian humanists (Alberti, Trithemius) were developing cipher systems.
Could theoretically generate artificial statistical profiles if cipher keys were complex.
counter_evidence: Homophonic ciphers increase entropy toward randomness (approaching 4.5+ bits); they do NOT lower entropy to 2.2 bits.
Fails every known cipher attack attempted by NSA, William Friedman, and modern supercomputers.

supporting_evidence: Rugg demonstrated that a Cardan grille over a syllable table can produce Voynich-like prefixes and suffixes.
Requires zero linguistic knowledge from the scribe.
counter_evidence: Disproven by Montemurro & Zanette (2013): Grille generation cannot create long-range topic clustering or legitimate Zipfian term-frequency networks.
Fails to explain the systematic Currier A vs Currier B dialect divergence across quires.

tier_2_theories.theory: Phonetic Dialect Transcription (Proto-Romance / Nahuatl / Hebrew / Turkic)
supporting_evidence: Superficial visual resemblances between isolated words and various foreign languages.
counter_evidence: Decisively disproven by the Oocephalus Test and Zodiac Star Concordance.
Every claimed phonetic translation (Bax, Cheshire, Tucker-Talbert) relies on cherry-picked words and violates internal grammar.
Natural spoken languages have character entropy ~4.0 bits, double that of Voynichese.
Disproven by AMS Radiocarbon dating (1404–1438 AD).
Disproven by McCrone micro-chemical pigment analysis.
Disproven by historical documentation in the 1639 Baresch letter and 1665 Marci letter to Kircher.
